title: 纽约大学设立乌克兰研究计划并加入全球学术联盟
body:
纽约大学正式设立乌克兰研究计划，内容涵盖学术课程、认证体系及网络研讨会系列。该计划由出生于基辅的纽约大学访问助理教授 Anastasiia Vlasenko 负责统筹。Vlasenko 指出，纽约大学凭借其学术资源、全球布局以及与乌克兰裔社区的深厚历史联系，成为研究乌克兰的理想机构。二战后约有六万名乌克兰人移居纽约，形成了毗邻校园且至今繁荣的“小乌克兰”社区。

该计划在美式教育项目中独具特色，将社会科学置于核心地位。纽约大学俄罗斯与斯拉夫研究系主席 Anne Lounsbery 教授表示，课程涵盖政治、历史、文学、电影、艺术及乌克兰语，不仅将乌克兰视为区域研究对象，更将其作为研究民主化、战时治理、国家认同及制度韧性的关键案例。学生可在俄罗斯与斯拉夫研究系、Wilf Family 政治系及国际关系项目中修读相关方向并获得证书。

纽约大学已加入由乌克兰第一夫人 Olena Zelenska 于2024年发起的“Global Coalition of Ukrainian Studies”。该联盟旨在联合全球高校深化对乌克兰的认知，成员包括维也纳大学、赫尔辛基大学及爱尔兰科克大学学院等。此外，学校还将与哥伦比亚大学 Harriman Institute 合作举办公开网络研讨会，进一步拓展学术交流边界。

此举延续了纽约大学在乌克兰相关领域的既有工作。自2022年起，纽约大学图书馆推出了乌克兰研究指南，整合历史与文明相关资源。同年，NYU Center for Responsible AI 与乌克兰天主教大学合作开展 RAI for Ukraine 项目，为受战争影响的学生提供负责任人工智能领域的研究机会与导师指导，多项成果已在顶级会议和期刊上发表。

# NYU Creates Ukrainian Studies Initiative

University joins international academic network backed by Ukrainian First Lady Olena Zelenska

Original publication date: 

* Interdisciplinary Impact
* Campus and Community
* Arts and Science

Cityscape of Kyiv, Ukraine on Independence Square. Photo credit: Mr-Tigga/Getty Images

New York University has established a Ukrainian Studies initiative, which will include academic programming and certification, a webinar series, and participation in the Global Coalition of Ukrainian Studies—an academic network launched by Olena Zelenska, the first lady of Ukraine.

“NYU’s academic offerings, its global presence, and its long-standing historic connections to Ukraine’s diaspora make the university a model institution for the study of Ukraine,” says [Anastasiia Vlasenko](https://as.nyu.edu/departments/ir/people/student-profiles/anastasiia-vlasenko.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1), an NYU visiting assistant professor who was raised in Kyiv and who will oversee the initiative. “Roughly 60,000 Ukrainians came to New York City after World War II, helping to establish the still-thriving Little Ukraine neighborhood that borders the NYU campus.”

“NYU’s Ukrainian Studies initiative is distinctive among American programs because it places the social sciences at the center,” adds Professor [Anne Lounsbery](https://as.nyu.edu/faculty/anne-l-lounsbery.html), chair of the university’s Department of Russian and Slavic Studies, pointing to course offerings in politics, history, literature, film, art, and the Ukrainian language. “It approaches Ukraine not solely as a subject of area studies, but as a central case for the study of democratization, wartime governance, national identity, and institutional resilience.”

NYU’s Ukrainian Studies initiative will encompass multiple components:

* A certificate in Ukrainian Studies
* A Ukrainian Studies track as part of study within NYU’s Department of Russian and Slavic Studies, Wilf Family Department of Politics, and International Relations program
* A public webinar series with Columbia University’s Harriman Institute

Earlier this month, NYU joined the Global Coalition of Ukrainian Studies, which aims to unite universities and research institutions in enhancing knowledge of Ukraine and in further developing Ukrainian studies. Other members include the University of Vienna, the University of Helsinki, and Ireland’s University College Cork. The organization was launched by First Lady Zelenska in 2024.

The initiative adds to NYU’s existing work linked to Ukraine:

* In 2022, NYU Libraries created a [Ukraine Research Guide](http://guides.nyu.edu/Ukraine), which assembles books, databases, digital repositories, news sources, and research institutions across Ukrainian history and civilization.
* Since 2022, the [NYU Center for Responsible AI](https://r-ai.co) has run [RAI for Ukraine](https://r-ai.co/ukraine) in partnership with Ukrainian Catholic University, providing students in Ukraine whose education has been disrupted by the war with access to high-quality research opportunities. The program connects students with mentors at academic institutions around the world for collaborative research in responsible AI, with numerous projects leading to peer-reviewed publications in top conferences and journals. Among these was a [study](https://engineering.nyu.edu/news/wars-educational-toll-nyu-tandon-research-reveals-78000-ukrainian-students-directly-impacted) that found Russia’s invasion of Ukraine displaced approximately 36,500 graduating high school students in 2022, 16 percent of the country’s senior class, while causing an additional 41,500 students to abandon the traditional pathway to higher education entirely during that year.

For more on the Ukrainian Studies initiative, please visit its [website](https://wp.nyu.edu/artsampscience-ukrainianstudies/).
